provisional_scope.central_question: How does the gut microbiome modulate the efficacy of immune checkpoint inhibitors in solid tumours, and what mechanisms mediate that effect?
cross_chapter_rules: Distinguish between observational associations (antibiotics) and interventional data (FMT) when discussing efficacy.
Explicitly note species differences (mouse vs. human) and tumor type specificity (e.g., melanoma vs. NSCLC) in all mechanistic claims.
Do not generalize metabolite effects (e.g., butyrate) without specifying context (ICI type, concentration, tumor type).
Highlight the absence of Phase III RCTs in Chapters 1 and 5 to manage expectations about clinical readiness.

material_theme_inventory.key_findings: Antibiotic exposure timing (pre- vs. post-ICI) significantly impacts survival; specific taxa (Fusicatenibacter, Butyricicoccus) associate with better OS in NSCLC.
Phase I/II trials show safety and potential efficacy (ORR up to 80% in NSCLC); mechanisms may involve pathobiont clearance rather than donor engraftment; safety risks (irAEs) vary by regimen.
Inosine, SCFAs, and bile acids modulate T cell function and tumor immunogenicity; direct human TME concentration data is limited.
Microbiome influences DC maturation, T cell priming, and myeloid cell suppression; ribosome biogenesis in host cells also plays a role.
FMT, probiotics, and diet show promise but lack standardization; Phase III RCT data is currently absent.

provisional_scope.provisional_scope: This review synthesizes evidence on the role of the gut microbiome in modulating immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) efficacy across solid tumours. It covers clinical associations (antibiotic exposure, FMT outcomes), microbial signatures (taxa, metabolites), mechanistic pathways (immune modulation, metabolic signaling, barrier integrity), and therapeutic interventions. The scope excludes hematological malignancies unless mechanistic insights are directly transferable to solid tumours. Emphasis is placed on human clinical data over preclinical models, with explicit notation of evidence grades (observational vs. interventional).
provisional_scope.review_title: Gut Microbiome Modulation of Immune Checkpoint Inhibitor Efficacy in Solid Tumours: Mechanisms and Clinical Evidence
